snmp_version_and_security_level.title: SNMP Version / Security Level
snmp_version_and_security_level.description: SNMP protocol version and (for v3) USM security level governing this monitoring flow. v1/v2c transmit the community string and all polled MIB data in cleartext with no message authentication or encryption; only v3_authpriv both authenticates (HMAC) and encrypts the payload. The cleartext values v1/v2c fire the cleartext-on-the-wire exposure, and the weak v3 levels v3_authnopriv/v3_noauth fire the weak-USM exposure; v3_authpriv and disabled are the secure non-firing states. Reuses the shared workspace enum so the gateway/component and this dataFlow name the same concept.

snmp_default_community_string_in_use.title: Default SNMP Community String In Use
snmp_default_community_string_in_use.description: Attestation that a vendor-default community string is accepted on the SNMP monitoring flow ('public' read / 'private' read-write, or another well-known default). net-snmp surfaces this as a 'rocommunity public' / 'rwcommunity private' (or com2sec) line, and on the wire as a successful 'snmpwalk -v2c -c public'. Modeled as an interpreted boolean so the trigger is polarity-safe. Fires (is_true) on the insecure flow; secure value is false (no default community accepted, ideally v3-only). Reuses the workspace name established by the monitoring-agent component.

snmp_community_string_strong_unique.title: SNMP Community String Strong and Unique
snmp_community_string_strong_unique.description: Attestation that any community string still in use on the flow is strong and unique - not a vendor default and not a guessable dictionary word (the secondary half of the default-community weakness: a non-'public' but trivially guessable community is exploited the same way a scanner sprays 'public'/'private'). Secure value is true (every community is high-entropy and unique, or - best - no community at all because the flow is SNMPv3-only); the exposure fires (is_false) when a weak/guessable community is accepted. Interpreted boolean, polarity-safe by construction.

snmpv3_uses_sha_and_aes_not_md5_des.title: SNMPv3 Uses SHA/AES, Not MD5/DES
snmpv3_uses_sha_and_aes_not_md5_des.description: Interpreted attestation that, where v3 priv is configured, the USM user is backed by SHA/SHA-2 authentication AND AES privacy rather than the deprecated MD5 auth / DES privacy primitives (createUser <user> SHA ... AES ...). Modeled as an interpreted boolean rather than a raw-string match so legacy primitive names cannot false-fire on a hardened config; fires (is_false) when MD5/DES legacy crypto is in use. Secure value is true.

known_vulnerabilities_patched.title: SNMP Agent Patched Against Known SNMP CVEs
known_vulnerabilities_patched.description: Interpreted attestation that the SNMP agent stack is patched current against known, exploitable SNMP defects - covering both the USM HMAC-length authentication bypass (CVE-2008-0960, where a client-supplied 1-byte HMAC length defeats authPriv/auth verification so a 'v3-secured' config is still authentication-bypassable: net-snmp 5.2/5.3/5.4 pre-fix and many vendor stacks) and known SNMP DoS defects (e.g. CVE-2025-20170 Cisco IOS/IOS XE improper error handling that lets an authenticated remote attacker reload the device, all SNMP versions). Fires (is_false) on an unpatched agent; secure value is true. A single shared patch-currency attribute that makes the cited CVEs assessable for both the weak-USM and amplification/DoS vectors. Aligns to the workspace patch-currency name.

snmp_write_community_disabled_or_acl_bou.title: SNMP Write Access Eliminated or ACL-Bound
snmp_write_community_disabled_or_acl_bou.description: Attestation that the SNMP monitoring flow grants no write (SET) access: no rwcommunity and no rwuser line is present, so only read access is granted. Monitoring must be read-only; a value of false (rwcommunity/rwuser present) turns the flow into a device-control channel where an attacker can change interface/route/ACL state or trigger a TFTP config download/upload - an authorization escalation. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when false. Aligns to the workspace SNMP write-access name.

snmp_mib_view_restricted_to_subtree.title: SNMP MIB View Restricted to Subtree
snmp_mib_view_restricted_to_subtree.description: Attestation that VACM restricts the polling user/community READ access to a needed OID subtree (net-snmp 'view'/'access' lines scoping READ to e.g. .1.3.6.1.2.1.1) rather than mapping it to the full MIB. True = scoped read view in place (secure). False = user/community mapped to the full '.1'/'.1.3'/'all' tree or a rouser with no -V view, so any authenticated poller or default-community holder reads the complete device inventory (interfaces, ARP/route tables, processes, installed software, sometimes config) - this insecure (false) state fires the exposure.

snmp_access_acl_restricted.title: SNMP Access ACL-Restricted
snmp_access_acl_restricted.description: Whether every SNMP access line restricts polling by source IP to the NMS (net-snmp SOURCE field on rocommunity/rwcommunity/com2sec, e.g. 'rocommunity secret 10.20.0.0/24', or rouser via VACM). Secure = true (every line names a specific NMS IP/subnet). Source ACL is also the primary control that defeats spoofed-source amplification because a spoofed victim source will not match the allow-list. Fires when false: a 'default'/blank SOURCE accepts any host that reaches the agent and holds the credential, and enables spoofed-source amplification. Shared canonical attribute referenced by both the network-exposure and amplification vectors; aligns to the workspace SNMP-ACL name.

snmp_agent_bound_to_management_interface.title: SNMP Agent Bound to Management Interface
snmp_agent_bound_to_management_interface.description: Whether 'agentaddress' pins UDP 161 to the management IP rather than binding all interfaces. Secure = true (agentaddress udp:<mgmt-ip>:161). Fires when false: the net-snmp default binds 161 on all IPv4 interfaces (absent directive or bare 'udp:161'), widening the reachable attack surface for the monitoring flow.

snmp_agent_internet_reachable.title: SNMP Agent Internet-Reachable
snmp_agent_internet_reachable.description: Whether UDP 161 of the SNMP agent is reachable from untrusted/internet networks (no firewall/host ACL confining it to management networks). Secure = false (port 161 filtered/closed from untrusted vantage points). Fires when true: an internet-reachable agent is both a device-takeover target and a reflection/amplification source. Shared canonical attribute referenced by both the network-exposure and amplification vectors (merged from the per-vector internet-reachable / internet-exposed phrasings).

snmp_agent_open_reflector.title: SNMP Agent Usable as Open Reflector
snmp_agent_open_reflector.description: Whether the agent answers GETBULK from arbitrary sources with a default/guessable community, making it usable as a spoofed-source UDP reflection/amplification vector (BAF ~6.3:1, higher on large tables; BITAG/Imperva). Secure = false (source ACL + non-exposure + no default community remove the open-reflector condition). Fires when true.

snmp_amplification_exposure_mitigated.title: SNMP Amplification Exposure Mitigated
snmp_amplification_exposure_mitigated.description: Attestation that the SNMP monitoring agent cannot be abused as a spoofed-source UDP reflection/amplification vector. Secure (true) when no anonymous/default-community GETBULK access is answerable from arbitrary sources (source-IP ACL + no default/public community + no untrusted-network exposure combine so a spoofed-source GETBULK with high max-repetitions cannot reflect an amplified response, BAF ~6.3:1 and higher on large tables, at a victim). Fires on false: the agent answers GETBULK from any source and is usable as an open amplifier. Kept distinct from the open-reflector attribute because this is the polarity-inverse (mitigated, fires is_false) trigger of the amplification vector and cannot be merged without breaking its condition.

response_rate_limiting_enabled.title: Response Rate Limiting Enabled
response_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Attestation that the agent (or fronting firewall/host ACL) rate-limits SNMP responses so a burst of GETBULK queries cannot sustain a high-volume reflected stream at a victim. Secure (true) when response rate limiting is in place; fires on false when no rate limiting caps the reflected/amplified traffic, leaving the agent able to sustain an amplification flood. Secondary structural mitigation per BITAG (rate-limit alongside source ACL and non-exposure). Aligns to the workspace response-rate-limiting name.

unauthenticated_v1_v2c_traps_accepted.title: Unauthenticated v1/v2c Traps Accepted
unauthenticated_v1_v2c_traps_accepted.description: Interpreted attestation: the NMS accepts SNMPv1/v2c traps (UDP 162) on this flow, configured via trapsink/trap2sink or informsink with a bare community. v1/v2c traps carry only a cleartext community and no message-origin authentication, so any host that can reach the NMS can forge a trap - masking genuine events, raising false alarms, or triggering automated (mis)remediation. Fires (true = insecure) when unauthenticated traps are accepted; secure value is false (no trapsink/trap2sink/community-only informsink).

snmp_traps_authenticated_v3_informs.title: Trap/Notification Channel Uses Authenticated v3 Informs
snmp_traps_authenticated_v3_informs.description: Interpreted attestation: asynchronous notifications on this flow use authenticated, encrypted SNMPv3 informs (trapsess -v 3 ... -l authPriv; informs preferred because they are acknowledged) rather than unauthenticated v1/v2c traps. authPriv informs provide the data-origin authentication and integrity that v1/v2c traps lack, so a forged trap cannot be injected into the NMS. Secure value is true; the exposure fires when this is false (no v3 authPriv notification channel).
